info.map.exports: Darker countries export more. The colour scale is clipped at the 95th percentile so a few giants do not wash out everyone else; hover for exact values.
info.map.imports: Darker countries import more. Imports here are valued free on board (without shipping and insurance), so they are a little lower than in national statistics.
info.map.balance: Blue: the country exports more than it imports (surplus). Red: it imports more (deficit). Grey: close to balance.
info.map.growth: Change in the value of exports against the previous year. Values are in current US dollars, so price swings (oil, metals) and exchange rates move them as much as volumes do.
info.worldTrend: The sum of all countries' exports of goods. Services are not included. Values are in current dollars, so the dips in 2009, 2015 and 2020 mix falling prices with falling volumes.
info.treemap: Each rectangle is a product chapter; its area is its share of trade. Colours group related chapters (food, fuels, chemicals, metals, machinery…).
info.fob: Exports and imports are both valued free on board (FOB) and reconciled between the two countries' reports, so they can differ from the country's own customs figures.
info.partners: Partners ranked by the value of goods traded this year. Open a partner to see both directions and the products behind them.
info.rca: RCA (revealed comparative advantage) compares a product's share in the country's exports with its share in world exports. RCA 2 means the product is twice as important for this country as for the world.
info.hhi: The Herfindahl–Hirschman index sums the squared shares. Below 0.15 exports are well diversified; above 0.25 they depend on a few partners or products.
info.imf: Monthly data from the IMF, which fills the gap until BACI's next annual release. Imports are valued CIF (including shipping and insurance), and the IMF includes estimates for countries that do not report monthly.
info.pair: Both lines come from the same reconciled dataset, so A's exports to B equal B's imports from A.
info.productTrend: The value of all countries' exports of this product. Price changes matter: for oil or metals, value can swing even when volumes are stable.
info.marketShare: Each line is a country's share of world exports of this product. Colours follow the country, ranked by today's size.
about.title: Methodology
about.lede: Where the numbers come from, how they are combined, and why they can differ from national statistics.
about.baci: bilateral trade by HS6 product, {first}–{last}, release V{version}. Built by CEPII from UN Comtrade, reconciling exporter and importer reports. Licence Etalab 2.0.
about.imf: monthly exports and imports by partner country, to {last}. Fills the gap until the next BACI release.
about.other: World Bank country classifications (CC BY 4.0), the HS 1992 nomenclature from UN Comtrade, and Natural Earth boundaries (public domain).
about.citation: Gaulier, G. and Zignago, S. (2010). BACI: International Trade Database at the Product-Level. The 1994–2007 Version. CEPII Working Paper 2010-23.
about.mirror.text: Each trade flow is reported twice — by the exporter and by the importer — and the two rarely agree. BACI reconciles them, weighting each country by how reliable its reports have been. Figures can therefore differ from a country's own published totals.
about.fob.text: Exports are valued free on board (FOB): the goods at the exporter's border. Imports are usually valued CIF, adding cost, insurance and freight. BACI reports everything FOB; IMF monthly imports are CIF, so they look a few percent higher.
about.rca.text: A product's share in a country's exports divided by its share in world exports (the Balassa index). RCA ≥ 1 means the country specialises in the product.
about.hhi.text: The Herfindahl–Hirschman index: the sum of squared shares, from 0 (spread across many) to 1 (all in one). Used for a country's partners and products, and for a product's exporters.
about.hs.text: The Harmonized System classifies goods in 21 sections, 97 chapters (2 digits), about 1,240 headings (4 digits) and 5,000 subheadings (6 digits). This site uses the 1992 edition throughout, so 30 years are comparable.
about.entities.text: Some countries reported jointly before a split: Belgium-Luxembourg until 1998, Sudan (with South Sudan) until 2011, Serbia and Montenegro until 2005. They are kept as separate entries and drawn on the map over their successor. Taiwan appears in BACI as "Other Asia, n.e.s.".
about.compare.title: Why sources differ: BACI vs IMF, {year}
about.compare.subtitle: Annual exports of the largest exporters in both sources
about.compare.info: Re-export hubs such as the Netherlands, Belgium, Singapore and the UAE count goods passing through their ports as their own exports; BACI attributes them to the country that produced them. Hong Kong is the extreme case. Where the IMF lacks partner detail (e.g. some oil exporters), BACI fills it from importers' reports.
about.pipeline: A Python pipeline downloads the sources into Parquet; a dbt project on DuckDB models them into staging, intermediate and mart tables (270 million rows at the product level), with tests that reconcile totals between layers and sources. The marts are exported as static files for this site. IMF months are refreshed automatically every month.

about.name: Why “Mirror Flows”: every trade flow is reported twice — once by the exporter and once by the importer, a mirror image that rarely matches. Reconciling those mirror flows is what makes the numbers on this site comparable.
